summary: In the United States, acitretin has a boxed warning—the strongest safety alert from the FDA—for liver harm and teratogenicity, which means it can cause birth defects [3][5]. Because of these risks, females who are pregnant, plan to become pregnant during treatment or within at least 3 years after stopping, or cannot use reliable birth control must not take this medication [5]. In human trials, some individuals developed yellowing of the skin or eyes alongside abnormal liver test results that later returned to normal after using the drug [5]. Additionally, risk ratings from a small computer model rather than human tests placed the drug at a medium score of 55 for liver issues and a low score of 20 for heart issues [M].
